The neural dissociations and hotspot findings summarized here come from animal experiments (Berridge & Robinson, 1998; Peciña & Berridge, 2005; Smith & Berridge, 2007; Mahler et al., 2007; Schultz et al., 1997).

Figure 21.3: Reward prediction error: schematic changes in dopamine-neuron firing. A: the cue does not yet predict reward, so the burst occurs at reward. B: a learned cue predicts reward. C: an expected reward is omitted. D: reward arrives later than expected. Zero represents baseline dopamine-neuron firing (Schultz et al., 1997; Hollerman & Schultz, 1998).

Figure 21.4: Certain versus uncertain reward. The dashed blue curve represents a 50% chance of reward and shows sustained anticipatory activity during the waiting period. At the outcome, firing briefly rises above baseline if reward appears (green) or dips below baseline if it is omitted (red). Zero represents baseline dopamine-neuron firing. Curves are schematic (Fiorillo et al., 2003).
